Solution written to `/home/kara/solution-board-completion-lost.md` and verified against the real `boardctl` tool in a scratch repo.

## Summary

**Root cause.** A tick is two non-atomic durable writes: `git commit` (work lands on `origin/Beta`), then `boardctl update <id> --status complete --commit-hash <sha>`. If the process dies in between, git is the ground truth but the board row stays `pending`/`in_progress`. The scheduler then treats the open row as a dispatch candidate — risking duplicate work.

**Fix (t565 reconciliation-as-pick).** Two scripts, both included in the doc:
- `detect-lost-completions.sh` — read-only; joins open board rows (`boardctl list --json`) against `git log --all --grep=<id|title>`; exits `10` when a lost completion is found. Wire this at the top of every tick before dispatch.
- `reconcile-lost-completion.sh` — verifies the row is open, the SHA exists/ancestors HEAD, is contained in `origin/Beta`, and mentions the task id; then closes the **existing** row via `boardctl update ... --status complete --commit-hash <real-sha>`. It only ever calls `update`; it never creates or re-dispatches.

**Verified** in `/tmp/boardlab/repo`:
- Reproduced: `TASK-777` left `in_progress` with commit `3227e11` on HEAD.
- Detector fired `LOST ... id-in-commit`, exit `10`.
- Reconciler closed it with the exact SHA; `task_completed` event appended; `doctor` = OK.
- Post-reconcile detector exit `0`; negative tests (already-complete, missing row, bogus SHA, unmerged divergent commit) all abort without touching dispatch.

Recommended hardening (also in doc §4.3): include the board JSONL files in the same commit as the work, so "commit exists" and "row closed" are equivalent.
